name: Virgin Money M Account for Business
description: No monthly charges and free basic transactions mean it won't quietly eat into your cashflow. You get everything you'd expect from a traditional bank — plus accounting software integration and an online dashboard for your business data, which saves real hours on admin.
pros: Good for managing your money with the M-Track dashboard
cons: Free account only for companies with annual turnover under £1 million
No branches in the South of England, Wales or Northern Ireland

name: Tide Business Account — Free
description: Tide takes the pain out of managing payments. You can charge customers via card reader, smartphone, payment links or the web — all from one place. If you're registering a new limited company, you can do it through Tide for just £24.99.
pros: Cashback and free bank transfers for 12 months when you apply via NerdWallet
Earn interest with a free savings account
cons: No branches

name: Revolut Basic Business Account
description: If your business crosses borders, Revolut carries a lot of useful kit. Spend in over 150 currencies and exchange £1,000 per month at the interbank rate — manage your money, charge customers and send payments across the globe all from one place.
cons: All accounts have a monthly fee
You cannot deposit cash or cheques
Accounts are not FSCS protected

name: Barclays Business Bank Account
description: Barclays gives you free basic transactions and no monthly fees for the first 12 months. If you're thinking about scaling, account holders can access savings on bookkeeping software, business insurance and more through Barclays's partner marketplace.
pros: Free access to FreshBooks accounting software
Help when you need it, thanks to extensive business support options
cons: Monthly fee of £8.50 after the first year

name: Wallester Business Free Account
description: A fee-free account for managing expenses and issuing virtual debit cards — a genuinely strong alternative to traditional business banking for startups and digital-first teams. If your business needs scalable card and expense management, Wallester is worth a look.
pros: Issue hundreds of business expense cards instantly
Great for international and remote teams
Smart budgeting and expense management tools
cons: No overdraft or business loan options
Mobile app has mixed reviews
Not covered by the FSCS protection scheme

name: WorldFirst Business Account
description: If your business is about to break into new markets, WorldFirst is worth considering. Receive payments in over 20 currencies without charge, and send in over 100. There's no set-up or monthly fee, and there's a potential sign-up bonus on top.
pros: Avoid foreign transaction fees in 15 currencies
cons: No overdraft facility
Some outgoing payments have fees
No FSCS protection

name: NatWest Start Up Business Account
description: NatWest's Startup Business Account gives you no monthly fees and free basic UK transactions for two years. That's a meaningful head start for a new business. You also get branches, a solid mobile app and free accounting software.
pros: Two years of free basic transactions
Manage accounts online, via app, branch, Post Office or phone
cons: No branches in Scotland or Northern Ireland

name: The Co-operative Bank Business Bank Account
description: A no-fee business account from a bank with a genuine ethical policy. Free unlimited access to the Go Get Paid app, integration with Sage, Xero and QuickBooks, and access to Clover payment terminals for £1 a month for the first 12 months.
pros: Account management online, by phone, via app or branch
Arranged business overdraft of up to £250,000
cons: No branches in Northern Ireland

name: Monzo Lite Business Account
description: Monzo's Lite Account is a free business account with simple ways to pay — including in-person contactless card payments. Around nine in 10 applications are accepted the same day. Digital receipts, transaction insights and 24/7 customer support come as standard.
pros: Same-day account opening for most customers
Great app, with genuinely helpful features
cons: No phone or branch banking
Business accounts not available to charities or partnerships
No accounting software integration with the Lite account

name: Lloyds Bank Business Account
description: If you value banking in branch and face-to-face customer support, Lloyds is a good shout. Branches right across England and Wales, plus Halifax and Bank of Scotland branches in Scotland and Northern Ireland. No monthly fees for 12 months.
transferFee: 100 electronic payments out free per month
cons: £8.50 monthly fee after the first year
Certain transactions have fees
